about: Cells that rest on one bound move together when it moves: narrowing a ceiling from a hundred to sixty turned cells red with nobody looking at them, some of them past the horizon of whoever signed it.
The effect is the bound's, not the order's: the same narrowing in two steps names exactly the same cells as in one.
No cell that does not rest on it moves, and no cell that rests on it and should move stays.
What a signature reaches is its rank: the cells that rest on the bound it moves, counted before it is moved.
One ceiling ranks sixty-six of a hundred cells; an origin that looked at one cell ranks one. A signature is worth what rests on it and nothing else.

cases.name: a hundred cells in three clusters, sixty-six of them resting on one ceiling
